title: Stand, Soldier of the Cross
description: Stand, Soldier of the Cross in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Edward Henry Bickersteth wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 407.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Stand, sol-dier of the Cross, Thy high al-le-giance claim And vow to hold the world but loss For Thy Re-deem-er’s name.

lines: And vow to hold the world but loss
Thy league with God be solemnized,
No more thine own, but Christ’s;
With all the saints of old,
The warfare may be sharp and long,
When faith casts every trophy down

licence: Public domain: Edward Henry Bickersteth died in 1906.
credits: Words by Edward Henry Bickersteth (1825–1906), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
